title: ELECT: Settling Identity Before Rendering for Scalable Story Visualization
abstract: arXiv:2610.15555v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training-free story visualization without reference images must preserve recurring entities across frames while scaling to long narratives. Existing methods typically maintain consistency by conditioning each frame on other frames of the same story, coupling generation time, VRAM, or both to story length. We introduce ELECT, which instead settles cross-frame identity before final rendering through a language-guided scene-entity mapping and stationary anchors elected from the model's own drafts. This makes the per-frame cost of the final rendering pass independent of story length. Joint attention exceeds 96 GB of VRAM at 32 scenes, whereas ELECT remains at 8.3 s per frame and under 20 GB VRAM from 10 to 1000 scenes. On the Story50 long-story benchmark, ELECT reaches 0.833 average Character Consistency Similarity (aCCS), compared with 0.826 for ten-round refinement, at one seventh of its generation cost, with lower text alignment (0.327

translated_title: ELECT：在渲染前确定身份一致性以实现可扩展的故事可视化
translated_abstract: 免训练且无需参考图像的故事可视化方法，必须在扩展至长篇叙事的同时保持跨帧重复实体的一致性。现有方法通常通过将每一帧条件化于同一故事的其他帧来维持一致性，这使得生成时间、显存占用或两者都与故事长度相耦合。我们提出了ELECT，它通过语言引导的场景-实体映射以及从模型自身草稿中选举出的固定锚点，在最终渲染之前解决跨帧身份一致性问题。这使得最终渲染过程的每帧成本与故事长度无关。联合注意力方法在32个场景时就会超过96 GB显存，而ELECT在10到1000个场景范围内保持每帧8.3秒的速度和低于20 GB的显存占用。在Story50长篇故事基准上，ELECT达到了0.833的平均角色一致性相似度（aCCS），而十轮迭代精炼方法为0.826，且ELECT的生成成本仅为其七分之一，文本对齐度更低（0.327…
tldr: ELECT通过语言引导的场景-实体映射和从模型草稿中选举出的固定锚点，在最终渲染前解决跨帧角色身份一致性问题，使每帧渲染成本与故事长度无关，从而实现高效可扩展的长篇故事可视化。
